items.text: Adults 21 and over may carry in public up to 2 ounces (about 57 g) of cannabis flower, 8 g of concentrate, and edibles (including lower-potency hemp edibles) with up to 800 mg of THC in total, and give the same amounts to another adult without payment (Minnesota Statutes 342.09). Use is allowed in a private home or yard, on private property not open to the public unless the owner bans it, and at licensed venues or events that permit on-site use. Use in a motor vehicle is banned, as is smoking or vaping wherever smoking is banned or where a minor would breathe it in.

Liquor stores may sell from 8 am to 10 pm Monday to Saturday and from 11 am to 6 pm on Sunday. They may not sell on Thanksgiving Day or Christmas Day, or after 8 pm on Christmas Eve. Bars and restaurants stop serving at 2 am (Minnesota Statutes 340A.504).

laws.rule: While a vehicle is moving or part of traffic (including stopped at a light), Minnesota drivers may not hold a phone or other wireless device, use it to read or send messages, make calls (including video calls), or view videos, photos, games or apps (Minnesota Statutes 169.475). Calls and messages by voice or hands-free, and navigation or audio, are allowed if the device is not held and nothing is typed. Emergency use is allowed.

laws.rule: Adults 21 and over may carry 2 ounces or less of adult-use cannabis flower in public, 8 grams or less of concentrate, and edibles with 800 milligrams or less of THC. Use is allowed in a private residence and its yard, on private property not open to the public (unless the owner bans it), and at licensed on-site consumption venues. Use in a motor vehicle is banned, as is smoking, aerosol or vapour use anywhere smoking is banned under section 144.414, and use or possession in public schools and state prisons (Minn. Stat. 342.09 subd. 1 and 2).

layers.authority: USDA Forest Service, Superior National Forest (Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness)
layers.process: Permits are required year-round for day and overnight visits. From 1 May to 30 September, overnight trips (paddle, motor or hiking) and motorised day trips need a quota permit (a daily limit per entry point), reserved on Recreation.gov (1-877-444-6777) or walk-in. Quota permits go on sale at 9:00 am Central Time on the last Wednesday of January. From 1 October to 30 April, overnight visitors and non-motorised day visitors use a free self-issued permit. Fees for overnight visits May to September: adults US$16 (about A$22.70), youth under 18 US$8 (about A$11.40), plus a US$6 reservation fee (about A$8.50) and a US$32 minimum deposit (about A$45). Cancel 3 or more days before for a full refund of fees. Maximum 9 people and 4 watercraft in a group. The permit must be carried at all times. Entry to Quetico Provincial Park in Canada needs its own permit and border checks. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.
